study.title: Prevalence of rare blood cancers in Europe
study.background: Substantial uncertainty surrounds the prevalence of rare blood cancers. Using real-world data, brought together as part of DARWIN EU®, we aim to estimate the prevalence of rare blood cancers in order to see if they still meet the condition to be classified as a rare disease.
study.aim: What is the prevalence of rare blood cancers in Europe?
objectives: To estimate the prevalence of follicular lymphoma between 1st January 2010 and the end of available data in data sources from across Europe, stratified by age and sex
To estimate the prevalence of diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma between 1 st January 2010 and the end of available data in data sources from across Europe, stratified by age and sex
To estimate the prevalence of multiple myeloma between 1st January 2010 and the end of available data in data sources from across Europe, stratified by age and sex
To estimate the prevalence of chronic lymphocytic leukaemia between 1st January 2010 and the end of available data in data sources from across Europe, stratified by age and sex
To estimate the prevalence of acute myeloid leukaemia between 1st January 2010 and the end of available data in data sources from across Europe, stratified by age and sex and sex
To estimate the prevalence of acute lymphocytic leukaemia between 1st January 2010 and the end of available data in data sources from across Europe, stratified by age and sex
